verifications.trial_text_on_default_tab_explanation: innerText substring match for 'TRIAL' on default tab traces to the unrelated 'REFER A MAKER · EARN 30 FREE TRIAL DAYS' referral card and the body copy 'we add 30 days to your current trial' — NOT from TrialBanner. data-testid='plus-trial-banner' is absent on every dashboard tab, confirming TrialBanner returns null for founders.

non_founder_regression_code_review: Verified via static code read of /app/frontend/src/pages/MakerDashboard/TrialBanner.jsx — early-return chain is preserved in order: (1) `if (isFounder(maker)) return null;` (lines 41–42), then (2) the original `if (!sub || !sub.is_in_trial || dismissed) return null;` (line 44). For a non-founder, isFounder(maker)===false so the function falls through to the original gate; the Plus trial reminder code path for non-founders is untouched. No need to spin up a fixture maker.
critical_code_review_comments: TrialBanner.jsx: founder gate (line 42) is placed AFTER the localStorage check inside useEffect AND BEFORE the subscription/dismissed gate — correct order. Component still owns its own fetch via fetchMakerMe(); no extra prop plumbing needed.

TrialBanner.jsx: useEffect reads `sessionStorage.getItem('cm_trial_banner_dismissed')` inside the same effect as the fetches — fine because dismissed default is false and the effect runs once on mount.

FounderBenefitsTab.jsx: Hard-coded `founderCommission = 3` is fine for now since the founder rate is product-locked at 3%, but if policy ever exposes founder_platform_fee_bps consider reading it from policy for consistency with plus/standard which DO read from policy bps fields.

FounderBenefitsTab.jsx: Subline copy 'Processing (3%) is the same for everyone.' uses `procRate.toFixed(0)` — if processing_fee_bps ever drifts off a whole-percent value (e.g. 275bps=2.75%) it would round to '3%' and be misleading. Low priority since 300bps is currently the steady-state.
No data-testid added to the rate tile's big-number `<div>`; current testids on the parent tiles ([founder-rate-tile|plus|standard]) are sufficient for the text-content assertion used in this run.

success_rate.frontend: 100% on every assertion in the review request
